title: Report a pet scam
summary: This page provides advice on how to protect yourself from pet scams and what steps to take if you suspect you have been scammed.
what_you_need: Be prepared for the cost of owning a pet
Understand your rights as a consumer
Research the breeder or business to avoid being scammed
Ensure the animal's microchip numbers are valid when you complete a search on the NSW Pet Registry
Buy directly from the breeder and not someone on-selling the animal

faqs.q: What should I do if I suspect I have been scammed?
faqs.a: Contact your financial institution as soon as possible and report the issue to Scamwatch to warn others.

faqs.q: What are some signs that a pet purchase might be a scam?
faqs.a: Be cautious if you receive a different animal than agreed, if the seller takes your money and you don't receive the animal, if you are asked to pay before seeing the pet, or if the price seems too low.

faqs.q: How can I ensure the pet I buy is legitimate?
faqs.a: Ask for photos and check them using a reverse image search. Ensure the animal's microchip numbers are valid by checking the NSW Pet Registry. Buy directly from the breeder, not someone reselling the animal.
